title: Geometric computation of compact-group weight multiplicities
notes: Weight multiplicities and restriction to subgroups are proposed as student topics; Guillemin--Sternberg are said to give an answer in principle.
statement: For a compact connected Lie group \(G\), an integral dominant weight \(\lambda\), and a maximal torus \(T\), determine \(m_\lambda(\nu)=\dim\operatorname{Hom}_T(\mathbb C_\nu,V_\lambda)\), and interpret it as a quantization of the symplectic reduction of the corresponding prequantized orbit.
reconstruction: The choice of a highest weight, prequantum bundle and reduction is our precise version of a topic, not a claim that the notebook states the general singular theorem.
fate: The notebook supplies circulation evidence for a preprint by March 1982. \citet{guilleminsternberg1982multiplicities} was published in October 1982; the Kähler result and the later general symplectic/singular extensions must be distinguished. \citet[Introduction and \S2.4]{meinrenkensjamaar1999singular} give the latter, with a July 1997 preprint preceding the 1999 publication.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: The compact prequantizable Hamiltonian case has an index-theoretic solution, including singular reductions in the specified Riemann--Roch sense. No new open problem is inferred from this student topic.

title: The unspecified hyperbolic multiplicity programme
notes: Hyperbolic algebras are described by a Cartan matrix having a negative eigenvalue; multiplicities and Macdonald are mentioned.
statement: A symmetrizable generalized Cartan matrix is hyperbolic only if it is indecomposable of indefinite type and every proper connected principal submatrix is of finite or affine type. A negative eigenvalue alone does not impose these conditions. No matrix, module, weight, or proposed multiplicity formula is specified.
fate: This is not enough to identify a single problem or match a later theorem. The general root-multiplicity discussion earlier this year and the compact-group problem are distinct. Search by the phrase and the cited surname yielded no uniquely recoverable target.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: The programme is identifiable by subject only; an exact fate cannot be assigned. No claim that hyperbolic multiplicities are generally uncomputed is made.

title: The regular SU(3) orbit and its hexagonal diagonal image
notes: The skew-Hermitian trace-zero matrix \(X\) has fixed \(\operatorname{tr}X^2=c_2\), \(\operatorname{tr}X^3=c_3\). Its orbit is six-dimensional and its diagonal projection is drawn as a hexagon.
statement: For three distinct real eigenvalues \(\lambda_1>\lambda_2>\lambda_3\), with sum zero, the orbit of \(i\operatorname{diag}(\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\lambda_3)\) is \(SU(3)/T^2\), of real dimension six. Its diagonal image is the convex hull of the six permutations of \(\lambda\). For repeated eigenvalues the orbit dimension and polygon degenerate.
reconstruction: Regularity and the ordered real eigenvalues make the sketch precise.
fate: \citet[Introduction and Theorem 1]{atiyah1982convexity} explicitly relate the general torus theorem to the older Schur--Horn and coadjoint-orbit cases. The notebook attributes the orbit picture to \citet{berezingelfand1956spherical}; that attribution is retained as a partial historical match, not evidence that every later quantization assertion is in the 1956 paper.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: the stated qualified result is established; the literal notebook shorthand should be read with the hypotheses above.

title: Dimensions and singular values of the torus moment map
notes: A regular fibre of the diagonal projection \(p\) has dimension four; the diagram marks internal walls where the fibre becomes singular.
statement: For the Hamiltonian action of the effective two-torus on a regular six-dimensional orbit, a regular level \(\mu^{-1}(\nu)\) has dimension four and its quotient by a locally free torus action has dimension two. Values with positive-dimensional isotropy are critical, including the boundary of the moment polygon; an interior-wall drawing is not a complete classification by itself.
reconstruction: The quotient and the qualification about the diagram are editorial additions.
fate: This is the regular-value theorem together with Hamiltonian reduction. \citet[\S2.1]{meinrenkensjamaar1999singular} distinguish the level set from its quotient and explain the stratification when regularity fails.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: the stated qualified result is established; the literal notebook shorthand should be read with the hypotheses above.

title: SU(3) weight hexagons and multiplicity layers
notes: Irreducible representations are indexed by two integers; a hexagonal weight diagram has increasing multiplicities towards a central triangle.
statement: For \(SU(3)\), dominant integral highest weights are \(a\omega_1+b\omega_2\), \(a,b\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\). Weight multiplicities are Weyl-invariant, have the familiar successive-layer pattern, and are bounded by \(\min(a,b)+1\). Only weights in the appropriate root-lattice coset occur; a drawn polygon does not make every lattice point a weight.
fate: The compact semisimple character formula in \citet{kirillov1968characters} provides the established representation-theoretic setting. The diagram is expository and does not constitute a new multiplicity theorem.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: The highest-weight classification and the type A2 multiplicity pattern are classical. The sketch is not a specification of a new formula.

title: Riemann–Roch multiplicity requires a reduced space
notes: The notes write \(X=p^{-1}(y_0)\) and \(\langle e^B\operatorname{Td},X\rangle=\text{multiplicity}\), for large parameters.
statement:
At a regular integral weight \(
u\), with a free effective torus action and the descended prequantum line bundle \(L_
u\), the relevant index is \(\int_{M_
u}\operatorname{ch}(L_
u)\operatorname{Td}(TM_
u)\), where \(M_
u=\mu^{-1}(
u)/T\). Appropriate positivity identifies this index with the relevant holomorphic multiplicity. Orbifold stabilizers require an orbifold index, and singular levels require a separately defined singular Riemann--Roch number.
reconstruction: We supply \(M_\nu\), the descended line bundle, and the index interpretation. The notebook does not justify using an ordinary Todd integral on a singular quotient.
fate: The 1982 Guillemin--Sternberg result and \citet[\S2.4]{meinrenkensjamaar1999singular} support the reduced-space interpretation. The scanned formula genuinely omits the quotient, so this is a faithful mathematical error rather than a translation slip.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: the stated qualified result is established; the literal notebook shorthand should be read with the hypotheses above.

title: An unspecified duality between groups and representations
notes: Gelfand calls the duality between groups and their representations the main question.
statement: No category of groups, dual object, topology, or universal property is specified. Pontryagin, Tannakian and orbit-method dualities are different possible interpretations.
fate: No exact theorem can be selected from this sentence without importing a programme into the record.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: The question remains a historical programme statement, not an indexed mathematical conjecture.
speaker: I. M. Gelfand

title: Falling factorials as a basis for finite differences
notes: Gelfand contrasts \(d(x^n)/dx=nx^{n-1}\) with \(\Delta x^{\underline n}=n x^{\underline{n-1}}\).
statement: For \(\Delta f(x)=f(x+1)-f(x)\) and \(x^{\underline n}=x(x-1)\cdots(x-n+1)\), \(\Delta x^{\underline n}=n x^{\underline{n-1}}\) for \(n\ge1\); equivalently \(\Delta\binom{x}{n}=\binom{x}{n-1}\).
fate: This follows immediately by factoring the two falling factorials. It is the classical Newton-series basis underlying \citet{mahler1958interpolation}, not a theorem originating in this talk.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: the stated qualified result is established; the literal notebook shorthand should be read with the hypotheses above.
speaker: I. M. Gelfand

title: Orbit volume and representation dimension need a normalization and a shift
notes: The invariant orbit measure is unique up to scale and can be normalized so that its volume is the representation dimension.
statement: On a compact homogeneous orbit the invariant measure is unique up to a positive scalar. Rescaling it to any prescribed positive total volume is tautologically possible. With the standard Kirillov--Kostant Liouville normalization, the dimension formula instead uses the orbit through \(\lambda+\rho\), not generally the unshifted orbit through \(\lambda\).
fate: The character formula of \citet{kirillov1968characters} is the relevant established source. The note is correct as a freedom to choose scale, but cannot by itself identify that scale with the canonical symplectic normalization.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: the stated qualified result is established; the literal notebook shorthand should be read with the hypotheses above.

title: Fractional differentiation and the Euler hypergeometric integral
notes: The displayed integral for the \(p\)-th derivative of \(x^k(1-x)^\ell\) has kernel \((x-t)^{-p-1}\) and no gamma prefactor.
statement: Initially for \(0<x<1\), \(\operatorname{Re}k>-1\) and \(\operatorname{Re}p<0\), define \[D^p f(x)=\frac1{\Gamma(-p)}\int_0^x(x-t)^{-p-1}f(t)\,dt.\] Then \[D^p[x^k(1-x)^\ell]=\frac{\Gamma(k+1)}{\Gamma(k-p+1)}x^{k-p}{}_2F_1(-\ell,k+1;k-p+1;x),\] with consistent branches and meromorphic continuation in the parameters. In particular \(D^p x^k=\Gamma(k+1)x^{k-p}/\Gamma(k-p+1)\).
reconstruction: The branch, convergence domain and normalized fractional operator are supplied here.
fate: The substitution \(t=xu\) reduces this directly to the classical Euler integral; compare \citet[Eq.~15.6.1]{nist2026hypergeometric}. The missing \(1/\Gamma(-p)\) is visible in the scan. Ordinary derivatives at nonnegative integral \(p\) require continuation or the corresponding fractional-calculus definition, not a divergent literal integral.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: the stated qualified result is established; the literal notebook shorthand should be read with the hypotheses above.
speaker: I. M. Gelfand

title: The programme of multivariable hypergeometric functions
notes: There is said to be no satisfactory theory of hypergeometric functions of several variables.
statement: This is an assessment of the state of a subject, without a specified class of differential systems or a criterion of completeness. A precise later framework is the \(A\)-hypergeometric system attached to an integer matrix and a complex parameter.
fate: \citet{gelfandzelevinskykapranov1989hypergeometric} developed a major framework, preceded by the 1987--1988 announcements listed in that paper. This is a thematic successor, not proof that every intended multivariable question was solved.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: Several precise multivariable theories are established; the unrestricted evaluative sentence has no single true-or-false resolution.
speaker: I. M. Gelfand

title: Atiyah convexity and the torus approach to representations
notes: Atiyah is cited for the convexity of the momentum image of a torus action; Khovanskii and Kazarnovskii are mentioned in relation to Newton polyhedra.
statement: For a Hamiltonian torus acting on a compact connected symplectic manifold, the moment-map image is a convex polytope, the convex hull of the images of the fixed-point components, and its fibres are connected. Compactness, connectedness and a genuine Hamiltonian moment map are essential.
reconstruction: The precise theorem is separated from the unformulated application programme.
fate: \citet[Theorems 1--2]{atiyah1982convexity}, received 27 March 1981 and published in 1982, gives the result; the previous-year item 1980-508.15 already records its circulation. The names of Khovanskii and Kazarnovskii identify an adjacent Newton-polyhedron programme, but no specific enumerative formula is stated here.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: the stated qualified result is established; the literal notebook shorthand should be read with the hypotheses above.

title: Relative Darboux theorem for a smooth submanifold
notes: If \(\omega_0|_{TN}=\omega_1|_{TN}\), then near each point of \(N\) a diffeomorphism fixing \(N\) pulls \(\omega_1\) back to \(\omega_0\).
statement: Let \(N\) be a smooth embedded submanifold of a smooth manifold and let \(\omega_0,\omega_1\) be symplectic forms near \(x\in N\), with equal pullbacks to \(N\). There are neighbourhood germs and a diffeomorphism germ \(g\), identity on \(N\), such that \(g^*\omega_1=\omega_0\). No constant-rank assumption on the restricted form is needed for this local statement.
reconstruction: We interpret the displayed U-to-U map as an equivalence of neighbourhood germs; one fixed invariant open set is unnecessary.
fate: \citet[Chapter 2, \S1.3, Theorem I and proof, pp.~24--25]{arnoldgivental1990symplectic} state and prove this result. The Russian chapter appeared in 1985 and the English version in 1990. The March 1982 notebook is earlier circulation evidence, not proof that the 1985 chapter was the first announcement.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: Established as the relative Darboux–Givental theorem; the cited proof covers precisely equality of pullbacks.

title: Moser’s deformation argument relative to a submanifold
notes: Choose \(g_t^*\omega_t=\omega_0\), differentiate, and solve an ordinary differential equation; a point gives Darboux.
statement: First align the two bilinear forms at the base point by a linear map fixing \(T_xN\). On a sufficiently small neighbourhood, the interpolating forms are nondegenerate. Choose a primitive of \(\omega_1-\omega_0\) that vanishes as an ambient covector along \(N\); solve \(\iota_{V_t}\omega_t=-\alpha\), so \(V_t|_N=0\), and integrate. Equality of pullbacks alone does not say the unadjusted straight-line path is nondegenerate.
reconstruction: The linear adjustment and vanishing of the primitive as an ambient covector are supplied proof details.
fate: The full relative argument is given in \citet[Chapter 2, \S1.3]{arnoldgivental1990symplectic}. The homotopy method is older; the cited source explains the preliminary linear adjustment omitted in the notebook.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: the stated qualified result is established; the literal notebook shorthand should be read with the hypotheses above.

title: When does a two-form extend to an ambient symplectic form?
notes: The question asks when a two-form is the restriction of a symplectic form; closedness is named. Gelfand asks first for the vector-space structure.
statement: Let \(N\subset M\) be a submanifold germ with \(\dim M\) even and let \(\beta\) be a smooth two-form on \(N\). It extends locally near \(x\) to a symplectic form on \(M\) if and only if \(d\beta=0\) near \(x\) and \(\dim\ker\beta_x\le\operatorname{codim}_M N\).
reconstruction: The ambient dimension and corank inequality are absent from the question and supplied from the later theorem.
fate: \citet[Chapter 2, \S1.3, Extension Theorem, p.~25]{arnoldgivental1990symplectic} gives the exact criterion. The pointwise algebraic question omits closedness legitimately, whereas a smooth symplectic extension cannot.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: The local smooth extension problem is solved with this criterion; it does not assert a global embedding theorem.

title: The symplectic space of oriented rays
notes: The space of straight lines in \(\mathbb R^3\) is symplectic and is identified in Arnold’s explanation with \(T^*\mathbb R^2\).
statement: The space of oriented affine lines in \(\mathbb R^3\) is globally \(T^*S^2\): direction \(u\in S^2\) and closest point \(v\perp u\). Reduction of the unit-speed geodesic flow supplies its canonical symplectic form. A direction chart gives \(T^*\mathbb R^2\) only locally. Reversing the line orientation is anti-symplectic, so the unoriented quotient is not endowed with this same symplectic form.
reconstruction: Orientation and the local meaning of the affine cotangent chart are necessary qualifications.
fate: \citet[Example 1]{givental1983lagrangian} explicitly identifies the reduced space as \(T^*S^{n-1}\). The result is standard before the talk; the later paper verifies the exact geometric context.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: the stated qualified result is established; the literal notebook shorthand should be read with the hypotheses above.

title: Extremals and the obstacle example
notes: The space of extremals of any variational problem is said to be symplectic; a point and a sphere produce a two-dimensional family.
statement: For a regular finite-dimensional first-order variational problem, the Legendre transform identifies local Cauchy data with a symplectic phase space. On a regular fixed-energy level one may reduce by the nonvanishing Hamiltonian flow. Families generated by a fixed initial point can then give Lagrangian subvarieties; obstacle tangencies can create singularities. Degenerate Lagrangians or singular quotients require a separate treatment.
reconstruction: Regularity, reduction, and genericity are explicit modern hypotheses not supplied by the notebook.
fate: \citet[Examples 1--2, Theorem and Corollary]{givental1983lagrangian}, received 19 July 1982 and published in 1983, connects generic obstacle singularities to open swallowtails. This supplies a concrete development of the example, not a proof of the unrestricted word “any”.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: the stated qualified result is established; the literal notebook shorthand should be read with the hypotheses above.

title: The symplectic odd binary-form representation
notes: The space of binary forms of degree \(2n-1\) has Darboux coefficients \(q_j,p_j\) and an \(SL_2(\mathbb R)\)-invariant \(\omega=\sum dp_j\wedge dq_j\).
statement: Write the dehomogenized polynomial as \[F(w)=\sum_{j=1}^n q_j\frac{w^{2n-j}}{(2n-j)!}+\sum_{j=1}^n(-1)^{n-j}p_j\frac{w^{j-1}}{(j-1)!}.\] The irreducible module \(\operatorname{Sym}^{2n-1}\mathbb R^2\) has an invariant nondegenerate alternating form, unique up to scalar; the displayed coefficient normalization makes it \(\sum dp_j\wedge dq_j\).
reconstruction: The alternating signs in the second sum fix the overwritten sign on P001017. Different Hamiltonian/sign conventions in the publication are equivalent after a coordinate sign change.
fate: \citet[Example 2]{givental1983lagrangian} publishes this representation and its use in singularity models. The representation-theoretic alternating form itself is classical; the application is developed in the subsequent paper.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: the stated qualified result is established; the literal notebook shorthand should be read with the hypotheses above.

title: Translation Hamiltonian and reduction by q1
notes: \(w\mapsto w+t\) is generated by \(h=q_n^2/2-q_{n-1}p_n-\cdots-q_1p_2\); \(q_1\) is a first integral and \(q_1=1,p_1=1\) are imposed.
statement: With \(\omega=\sum dp_j\wedge dq_j\) and \(\iota_{X_h}\omega=dh\), the translation flow has \(\dot q_1=0\), \(\dot q_j=q_{j-1}\) for \(j>1\), \(\dot p_n=q_n\), and \(\dot p_j=-p_{j+1}\) for \(j<n\). The hypersurface \(q_1=1\) has characteristic direction \(\partial_{p_1}\); its quotient is symplectic of dimension \(2n-2\). Fixing \(p_1=1\) chooses a slice, rather than a second conserved quantity.
reconstruction: The Hamiltonian sign convention and the quotient meaning of the slice are supplied.
fate: \citet[Example 2]{givental1983lagrangian} gives the corresponding Hamiltonian representation and reduction. Direct coefficient differentiation of \(F(w+t)\) checks the notebook signs under the stated convention.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: The construction is established; no claim that p1 is preserved by the translation Hamiltonian is justified.

title: Goldsheid’s uniform approximation by coordinate-product Lagrangians
notes: Goldsheid asks whether every Lagrangian \(L\subset\mathbb R^{2n}\) admits \(L_1=\operatorname{span}(\alpha_je_j+\beta_jf_j)\) with \(\|P_L-P_{L_1}\|\le1/\sqrt2\); even any constant less than one independent of \(n\) would suffice.
statement: Use the standard Euclidean and symplectic structures, with \(Je_j=f_j\). Must every Lagrangian \(n\)-plane admit one nonzero vector in each prescribed coordinate plane \(\operatorname{span}(e_j,f_j)\), whose direct sum \(K\) satisfies \(\|P_L-P_K\|_{2\to2}\le2^{-1/2}\)? The weaker question asks for a universal \(c<1\) for all \(n\).
fate: The scan unambiguously gives an operator norm and a dimension-independent requirement. Searches under Goldsheid/Goldsheyd/\ru{Гольдшейд}, Lagrangian projections, symmetric-unitary diagonal approximation, Math-Net author records, arXiv and MathOverflow located no exact resolution. \citet[Theorem 3.4]{mehrmannpoloni2012doubling} bounds individual entries of a permuted Lagrangian graph basis; that does not supply the requested uniform operator norm. The development below proves a Fourier-matrix counterexample to the sharp constant at \(n=6\), a universal lower obstruction \(\cos(\pi/8)\), and a dimension-dependent upper bound.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: We disprove the proposed \(1/\sqrt2\) constant in dimension \(n=6\). More generally, any universal constant must be at least \(\cos(\pi/8)\). We establish \(\cos(\pi/(2n))<1\) for each fixed \(n\), but do not resolve the existence of a universal \(c\in[\cos(\pi/8),1)\). No exact later resolution of that weaker question was located in this bounded search.
worth: Worth developing because the exact finite-dimensional optimization is explicit and admits certified partial bounds while preserving the unresolved uniform quantifier.
speaker: I. Ya. Goldsheid

title: Coordinatewise closeness does not control the gap of the spans
notes: For every \(j\), one can choose \(\varphi_j=\alpha_je_j+\beta_jf_j\) with \(\sin\angle(\varphi_j,L)\le1/\sqrt2\).
statement: The compression of \(P_L\) to each coordinate \(J\)-plane has trace one, so its largest eigenvalue is at least \(1/2\), proving the coordinatewise claim. This supplies no bound for all linear combinations of the chosen vectors. Indeed for \(n\ge2\), \(v=(1,\ldots,1)/\sqrt n\) and \(L=\mathbb Rv\oplus i v^\perp\) give \(\operatorname{dist}(f_j,L)=1/\sqrt n\), yet \(\|P_L-P_{i\mathbb R^n}\|=1\).
reconstruction: The trace proof and the example separating the quantifiers are ours.
fate: The observation in the notebook is correct. The explicit counterexample to the inference about the span is proved and independently checked in our development; it is not a counterexample to Goldsheid’s existential question.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: The elementary coordinatewise statement is verified; its use as a proof of uniform subspace approximation would be invalid.

title: The index as an integral of a local density
notes: For an elliptic differential system \(D\), possibly on a manifold with boundary, \(\operatorname{ind}D=\int_M\alpha_0\) is attributed to Atiyah--Singer.
statement: For an elliptic differential operator \(D:C^\infty(E)\to C^\infty(F)\) on a closed compact manifold, the Fredholm index equals the integral of the constant coefficient in the local heat supertrace. On a manifold with boundary one must first specify an elliptic boundary realization; its formula generally includes boundary terms.
reconstruction: We allow different source and target bundles and separate the closed case from boundary realizations.
fate: This is an established index/heat-kernel theorem; \citet[Chapter 1, \S1.7]{gilkey1984invariance} gives the analytic formulation, while \citet[Theorem (3.10)]{atiyahpatodisinger1975spectral1} exhibit the boundary correction. A bare differential expression on a manifold with boundary does not have the asserted Fredholm index.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: the stated qualified result is established; the literal notebook shorthand should be read with the hypotheses above.

title: Meromorphic continuation of a positive elliptic zeta function
notes: For \(A=D^*D\) or \(DD^*\), poles are listed at \((n-j)/m\), with none at \(0,-1,-2,\ldots\).
statement: Let \(A\) be a positive self-adjoint elliptic differential operator of order \(m>0\) on a closed \(n\)-manifold, with zero eigenvalues omitted. Then \(\zeta_A(s)=\sum_{\lambda>0}\lambda^{-s}\) converges for \(\operatorname{Re}s>n/m\), extends meromorphically with at most simple poles at \((n-j)/m\), and is regular at nonpositive integers. Some candidate poles vanish. General classical pseudodifferential operators need a more qualified statement.
reconstruction: Closedness, differential order, positivity, omission of the kernel and ``possible poles are essential additions.
fate: This is classical complex-power/heat asymptotics: \citet{seeley1968powers} is the 1968 Russian translation of earlier work, and \citet[\S1.10]{gilkey1984invariance} supplies the heat formulation. It continues the expository item 1972-296.1.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: the stated qualified result is established; the literal notebook shorthand should be read with the hypotheses above.

title: The shifted-zeta formula for the index
notes: \(\operatorname{ind}D=\zeta_{1+D^*D}(0)-\zeta_{1+DD^*}(0)\).
statement: For a closed elliptic Fredholm realization, the positive eigenvalues of \(D^*D\) and \(DD^*\) agree with multiplicity. Therefore for every \(\varepsilon>0\), \[\zeta_{\varepsilon+D^*D}(s)-\zeta_{\varepsilon+DD^*}(s)=\varepsilon^{-s}\operatorname{ind}D\] first in a convergent half-plane and then by continuation; evaluation at zero gives the notebook formula.
reconstruction: The displayed all-s identity is our explanatory derivation, not a second formula claimed to be in the notes.
fate: The equality is an elementary spectral-pairing consequence of the heat-index method, as in \citet[\S1.7]{gilkey1984invariance}. It avoids the missing-kernel problem of unshifted zeta functions.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: the stated qualified result is established; the literal notebook shorthand should be read with the hypotheses above.

title: Local zeta values from a parameter-dependent parametrix
notes: Equation (5) integrates \(b^\circ_{-m-n}(x,\xi,\lambda)\) over \(|\xi|=1\) and a ray, with a minus sign and factor \(1/m\); it is a density.
statement: For an invertible positive elliptic differential \(A\), if \(\operatorname{tr}K_A(t;x,x)\sim\sum_j a_j(x)t^{(j-n)/m}\), then \(\zeta_A(0;x)=a_n(x)\). If zero modes are omitted, subtract the kernel-projection density. The coefficient is computed from the homogeneous degree \(-m-n\) resolvent symbol, using an admissible ray and a fixed convention for \((A-\lambda)^{-1}\), Fourier factors and contour orientation.
reconstruction: We supply a convention-independent heat statement and preserve the resolvent formula as a separate, convention-sensitive notebook assertion.
fate: The heat version is verified in \citet[\S1.10]{gilkey1984invariance}. The parametrix expression belongs to the Seeley/Wodzicki calculus; the notebook alone does not fix enough conventions to certify a sign error in Seeley. The stronger assertion of cut-independent pointwise density is not valid for arbitrary pseudodifferential operators; compare \citet[Remark 4.4]{ponge2006spectral}.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: the stated qualified result is established; the literal notebook shorthand should be read with the hypotheses above.

title: The signature operator and its chirality splitting
notes: The notes introduce \(D=(d+d^*)|_{\Omega_+}\), with a phase times the Hodge star, and identify its index with the signature.
statement: On a closed oriented Riemannian manifold of dimension \(4k\), the Hodge-star phase defines the standard chirality involution on complex differential forms; \(d+d^*\) interchanges its eigensubbundles. The index of its positive-to-negative part, with the compatible chirality convention, is the signature of the middle-dimensional intersection pairing.
reconstruction: The notebook phase uses an insufficiently specified n; we do not silently replace it by a different exponent. The modern statement specifies the standard chirality by its operator properties.
fate: This is the classical signature operator. \citet[Chapter 3, \S3.1]{gilkey1984invariance} fixes the chirality convention; \citet[\S4]{atiyahpatodisinger1975spectral1} explain the boundary modification. The preceding scanned hypothesis \(\partial M\ne\varnothing\) cannot accompany the uncorrected integral equality.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: the stated qualified result is established; the literal notebook shorthand should be read with the hypotheses above.

title: The div–grad–curl example and its missing sign
notes: Gelfand writes \(\bigl(\begin{smallmatrix}0&\operatorname{div}\\\operatorname{grad}&\operatorname{rot}\end{smallmatrix}\bigr)^2=\Delta I\), with a parenthetical \(\mathbb R^4\).
statement: Using the usual Euclidean operators on \(\mathbb R^3\), the literal square is \(\operatorname{diag}(\Delta,2\operatorname{grad}\operatorname{div}-\Delta I_3)\). A self-adjoint Dirac-type version is \[B=\begin{pmatrix}0&-\operatorname{div}\\\operatorname{grad}&\operatorname{curl}\end{pmatrix},\qquad B^2=-\Delta I_4.\] The four refers to a scalar plus three vector components, not a four-dimensional base.
reconstruction: We explicitly fix the conventional Euclidean signs instead of treating the shorthand as a literal self-adjoint matrix identity.
fate: \citet[Introduction, p.~45]{atiyahpatodisinger1975spectral1} discuss the same operator only up to sign conventions. Our vector-calculus calculation and the repeated \(\mathbb R^3\) wording on P001024 settle the notebook ambiguity; the accompanying symbolic check is included.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: the stated qualified result is established; the literal notebook shorthand should be read with the hypotheses above.
speaker: I. M. Gelfand

title: Local signature and Todd densities
notes: Atiyah--Bott--Patodi identify \(\alpha_0\) with \(L_k(p)\), in dimension four \(p_1/3\); for \(\bar\partial\), a Kähler assumption is stated for the Todd density.
statement: For the geometric signature operator the constant heat supertrace density is the top-degree Hirzebruch \(L\)-form. For the Dolbeault complex with the usual Kähler metric and compatible Hermitian connection, the local index density is the appropriate Todd form (and the Chern character for coefficients). Equality of integrated characteristic numbers does not make arbitrary pointwise representatives identical.
fate: \citet{atiyahbottpatodi1973heat} is the 1973 publication named by the talk. \citet[Chapter 3, \S\S3.1 and 3.6--3.7]{gilkey1984invariance} provides the precise geometric versions. The notebook correctly warns against dropping the Kähler qualification in its stated pointwise formula.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: the stated qualified result is established; the literal notebook shorthand should be read with the hypotheses above.

title: The signature theorem with its eta boundary correction
notes: \(\operatorname{sign}M=\int_M L_k(p)-\eta(\partial M)\), for a product metric near the boundary.
statement: For compact oriented Riemannian \(M^{4k}\), product near \(Y=\partial M\), define the signature on the image of \(H^{2k}(M,Y;\mathbb R)\to H^{2k}(M;\mathbb R)\). With the APS odd-signature operator on even forms and its boundary orientation, \[\operatorname{sign}M=\int_M L-\eta(B_Y;0).\] This normalization is different from writing \((\eta+h)/2\) for a general Dirac boundary problem.
fate: \citet[Theorem (4.14)]{atiyahpatodisinger1975spectral1} is the exact result. Its announcement appeared in 1973, the full paper was received 25 March 1974, and publication followed in 1975; the notebook’s ``1974 should not replace those distinct dates.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: the stated qualified result is established; the literal notebook shorthand should be read with the hypotheses above.

title: Is signature the only additive invariant?
notes: Gelfand asks whether signature is the unique additive invariant of manifolds with boundary.
statement: “Additive” has no specified gluing category or normalization here. Under gluing compact even-dimensional manifolds along complete closed odd-dimensional boundary components, Euler characteristic is also additive, since \(\chi(M\cup_YN)=\chi(M)+\chi(N)-\chi(Y)\) and \(\chi(Y)=0\). It is independent of signature: \(\chi(D^{4k})=1\), \(\sigma(D^{4k})=0\). If orientation-oddness or cobordism invariance is imposed, that is a different question.
reconstruction: The Euler-characteristic example refutes only the plainly stated broad interpretation; no extra axiom is attributed to Gelfand.
fate: \citet[Chapter 1, Corollary (1.4)]{karraskreckneumannossa1973cutting} already classify the corresponding real-valued cut-and-paste invariants of closed oriented manifolds by Euler characteristic and signature. This is useful context, not an exact match to an unstated boundary gluing law.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: The broad uniqueness interpretation is false, while the intended restricted axioms cannot be recovered from this line.
speaker: I. M. Gelfand

title: Filling independence and nonlocality of the signature defect
notes: Doubling shows that \(\eta(\partial M)\) is independent of the filling; lens spaces show it is nonlocal because it fails multiplicativity under coverings.
statement: For two product-metric fillings of the same oriented metric boundary, glue one to the orientation reverse of the other and apply the closed signature theorem and signature additivity. Their defects \(\int L-\sigma\) agree. A universal natural local boundary-density integral would multiply under finite local-isometry coverings; the signature eta invariant need not do so.
reconstruction: Two possibly different fillings, common boundary metric and orientation reversal make the gluing argument precise.
fate: \citet[Introduction, pp.~43--45]{atiyahpatodisinger1975spectral1} give exactly this motivation and the sphere/lens-space obstruction. Filling independence does not say eta is independent of the boundary metric.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: the stated qualified result is established; the literal notebook shorthand should be read with the hypotheses above.

title: Spectral boundary projections and the normal-operator qualification
notes: Near the boundary \(D=\partial_u+A\), with \(A\) normal and spectrum outside a cone near \(i\mathbb R\); \(P_A\) projects to \(\operatorname{Re}\lambda\ge0\). Local elliptic boundary conditions need not exist.
statement: The classical APS construction assumes \(D=\sigma(\partial_u+A)\) in a product collar, where \(\sigma:E|_Y\to F|_Y\) is an isomorphism and \(A\) is self-adjoint elliptic on \(E|_Y\). Requiring \(P_{\ge0}(A)(f|_Y)=0\) gives an elliptic Fredholm realization. More general sectorial projections require symbol cuts and resolvent estimates; normality plus a bare spectral drawing is not a complete analytic hypothesis list.
reconstruction: The modern statement deliberately separates the proved classical boundary theorem from the notebook’s larger normal-operator claim.
fate: \citet[\S2 and Theorem (3.10)]{atiyahpatodisinger1975spectral1} verify the self-adjoint case. \citet[\S3 and Appendix A]{ponge2006spectral} provide the modern spectral-cut framework, not by themselves a proof of this entire normal-boundary index assertion.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: the stated qualified result is established; the literal notebook shorthand should be read with the hypotheses above.

title: APS index formula and the role of the zero modes
notes: \(\operatorname{ind}D=\int\alpha_0-(h_0+\eta(A))/2\); \(h_0\) counts purely imaginary eigenvalues, while the notes explicitly say APS used self-adjoint \(A\).
statement: Under the classical self-adjoint product-collar assumptions, \[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ind}D_{\mathrm{APS}}&=\int_M\alpha_0-\frac{\eta_A(0)+\dim\ker A}{2},\\ \eta_A(s)&=\sum_{\lambda\ne0}\operatorname{sign}(\lambda)|\lambda|^{-s}.\end{aligned}\] The choice to exclude nonnegative boundary eigenmodes determines the kernel term; changing the zero-mode boundary subspace changes the index.
reconstruction: The precise theorem assumes self-adjointness. The manuscript’s distinction is retained.
fate: \citet[Theorem (3.10)]{atiyahpatodisinger1975spectral1} proves this formula. The normal-operator expression using \(\operatorname{Re}\lambda\) is a proposed extension with only a partial publication match here. It is not silently substituted into the original APS theorem.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: the stated qualified result is established; the literal notebook shorthand should be read with the hypotheses above.

title: Variation of the signature eta invariant on a cylinder
notes: \(\int_{N\times I}L_k(p)=\eta_{p_1}-\eta_{p_2}\) is written below a cylinder diagram.
statement: For an oriented cylinder of dimension \(4k\), with product metrics at both ends, its signature is zero. Applying the signature boundary theorem yields that its \(L\)-integral equals the signed difference of the two boundary eta invariants, with signs determined by outward boundary orientation. For a general family of self-adjoint elliptic operators, an analogous formula requires the spectral-flow/kernel terms.
reconstruction: The theorem is restricted to the geometric signature situation actually illustrated; the indices p or rho in the manuscript are not interpreted as additional data.
fate: The signature case follows directly from \citet[Theorem (4.14)]{atiyahpatodisinger1975spectral1}. The source says only “elliptic operator” at this point; a general family formula cannot be inferred by omitting integer jumps.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: the stated qualified result is established; the literal notebook shorthand should be read with the hypotheses above.

title: The collar operator and boundary bundle identification
notes: \(D:E\to F\) is written as \(\partial_u+A\), while \(A:E|_Y\to F|_Y\) is then assigned eigenspaces.
statement: Factor the invertible normal symbol: \(D=\sigma(\partial_u+A)\). Then \(A\) is an operator on the single boundary bundle \(E|_Y\), after identifying the target by \(\sigma^{-1}\). Its nonnegative spectral projection can act on \(f|_Y\). Without this identification, an operator between distinct bundles has no intrinsic spectrum.
reconstruction: The missing normal-symbol isomorphism is supplied, not read from the scan.
fate: This factorization is explicit in \citet[Theorem (3.10)]{atiyahpatodisinger1975spectral1}. The notebook suppresses \(\sigma\), a harmless shorthand only if the bundle identification is supplied.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: the stated qualified result is established; the literal notebook shorthand should be read with the hypotheses above.

title: The repeated APS formula and the choice of projection
notes: \(P_+f|_Y=0\) and \(\operatorname{ind}D=\int\alpha_0-(h+\eta)/2\) are repeated for normal \(A\).
statement: For self-adjoint \(A\), the displayed \(-h/2\) formula corresponds to \(P_{\ge0}\), not the strictly positive projection alone. For \(P_{>0}\), allowing the kernel changes the index by \(h\). The normal case requires an explicitly chosen imaginary-axis spectral subspace and additional analytic hypotheses.
reconstruction: We distinguish positive from nonnegative and do not claim to have proved the full normal-operator extension.
fate: \citet[Theorem (3.10)]{atiyahpatodisinger1975spectral1} verifies the nonnegative convention. This record is a genuine repeated occurrence of 1981-558.11--12; it should remain linked rather than counted as a second independent discovery.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: the stated qualified result is established; the literal notebook shorthand should be read with the hypotheses above.

title: Heat supertrace as the basis of the boundary index proof
notes: Equation (9) writes \(\operatorname{ind}D=\operatorname{Tr}e^{-tD^*D}-\operatorname{Tr}e^{-tDD^*}\).
statement: For a closed densely defined Fredholm operator with compact-resolvent nonnegative realizations \(D^*D\) and \(DD^*\), positive eigenvalues pair under \(D\), so their heat-trace difference equals the index for every \(t>0\). For a boundary problem, \(D^*\) must be the adjoint of the chosen APS realization, with its corresponding complementary boundary condition.
reconstruction: The operator domains are indispensable supplied hypotheses.
fate: \citet[\S3]{atiyahpatodisinger1975spectral1} use this identity in the boundary calculation. The formula is older than the talk and is not valid for two independently chosen boundary domains.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: the stated qualified result is established; the literal notebook shorthand should be read with the hypotheses above.

title: Positive spectral zeta: a zero global residue can have a nonzero local density
notes: \(\zeta_+(s)=\sum_{\lambda>0}\lambda^{-s}=\operatorname{Tr}(P_+A^{-s})\) has a finite value at zero, although its local density may have a residue whose integral is zero.
statement: For a self-adjoint classical elliptic operator of positive order on a closed manifold, \(\zeta_+(s)=\operatorname{Tr}(P_+|A|^{-s})\) is regular at zero. The meromorphic diagonal trace density can have a nonzero pointwise residue; its integral vanishes. Thus regularity of a global trace does not establish pointwise holomorphy.
reconstruction: We use absolute values on the spectral powers and specify closedness and classical order.
fate: \citet[Theorem 0.1 and Introduction]{gilkey1981residue} establish global eta regularity in all dimensions and discuss nonzero local residues. Together with zeta regularity this gives the positive part. \citet[Theorem 4.3 and Remarks 4.4--4.5]{ponge2006spectral} explain the residue of projections. Gilkey’s 1981 publication precedes this talk.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: the stated qualified result is established; the literal notebook shorthand should be read with the hypotheses above.

title: The sum and difference of the two spectral halves
notes: \(\zeta(A)=\zeta_+(A)+\zeta_-(A)\), \(\eta(A)=\zeta_+(A)-\zeta_-(A)\).
statement: For real nonzero spectrum define \(\zeta_\pm(s)=\sum_{\pm\lambda>0}|\lambda|^{-s}\). Then \(\zeta_{|A|}(s)=\zeta_+(s)+\zeta_-(s)\) and \(\eta_A(s)=\zeta_+(s)-\zeta_-(s)\). A spectral-cut zeta function of \(A\), rather than \(|A|\), has a phase on the negative part. At zero those phases can be discarded only after checking the regularity just discussed.
reconstruction: We separate functions from their regularized values at zero and make the hidden absolute-value convention explicit.
fate: The distinction is explicit in \citet[\S4, equations (4.1)--(4.2)]{ponge2006spectral}. The notebook writes values at zero; extending its first equality to all \(s\) without \(|A|\) would be false.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: the stated qualified result is established; the literal notebook shorthand should be read with the hypotheses above.

title: Boundary values for unspecified general characteristic classes
notes: Gelfand cites Gabrielov, Gelfand and Fuks for algebraic reasons for nonlocality and says the analogous task for general classes has not been done.
statement: The class of characteristic classes, geometric structures, equivalence relation on boundary data and desired invariant are unspecified. The sentence does not determine a unique generalization of the signature eta invariant.
fate: The adjacent Pontryagin discussion suggests characteristic-class transgression, but is not enough to identify a theorem. The well-known Gabrielov--Gelfand--Losik papers must not be silently substituted for the name \ru{Фукс} actually visible in the scan; the attribution remains unresolved.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: No precise new open problem or exact later solution can be assigned without additional source evidence.
speaker: I. M. Gelfand

title: Stredder and Epstein: an identifiable bibliographic pointer
notes: Two papers by Stredder and Epstein are listed as J. Differential Geometry 10 (1975), 645, about natural differential operators.
statement: The identifiable works are Epstein, “Natural tensors on Riemannian manifolds”, pp.~631--645, and Stredder, “Natural differential operators on Riemannian manifolds and representations of the orthogonal and special orthogonal groups”, pp.~647--660. No particular classification theorem is stated in the seminar notes.
fate: The two titles and page ranges are independently recorded in the reference list of \citet{fegansteer2005second}. The original DOI/Project Euclid routes did not open in this run, so the two original entries are marked unverified and the verification level remains indirect. Page 645 is the end of Epstein’s paper, not a common starting page.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: The bibliographic pointer is identified; no full-text verification of either original classification is claimed.

title: Is self-adjointness necessary for spectral asymmetry?
notes: Gelfand asks \ru{зачем самосопряженность A?}; the subsequent construction uses complex spectral cuts.
statement: For a positive-order classical elliptic operator on a closed manifold, complex powers and a zeta function can be defined without self-adjointness when a ray avoids both the principal-symbol spectrum and the operator spectrum and satisfies the required parameter-dependent resolvent estimates. Replacing a real-sign eta sum requires specifying the cut or sector; it is not the same definition without choices.
reconstruction: We answer the closed-operator functional-calculus question precisely. The broader normal boundary index assertion in 1981-559.2 is not proved by this answer.
fate: Seeley’s complex-power theory predates the talk; \citet{seeley1968powers} is an early published translation. \citet[\S\S2--4]{ponge2006spectral} give the later precise asymmetry comparison. Wodzicki’s relevant papers appeared in February 1982 and February 1984; the closed-manifold construction is not an unresolved question of principle.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: Self-adjointness is unnecessary for admissible-cut complex powers. The choice dependence and boundary-domain issues must be specified separately.
speaker: I. M. Gelfand

title: Does eta regularity require a filling?
notes: An eta invariant is described through a filling and the notes say the case without a filling has not been proved.
statement: For every self-adjoint classical elliptic operator of positive order on a closed manifold, in any dimension, the eta function has a meromorphic continuation regular at zero. Its spectral definition needs no bounding manifold. A geometric filling can give an index formula for its value but is not required for existence.
reconstruction: The ambiguity between self-adjoint regularity and the normal extension is retained rather than resolved by attribution.
fate: \citet[Theorem 0.1]{gilkey1981residue} proves the general regularity, following the earlier odd-dimensional APS result. The notebook sentence is false if read as a claim about all such self-adjoint operators; it may instead refer to the unspecified nonself-adjoint extension. Earlier occurrences are 1972-296.2--3 and 1972-296.5.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: The self-adjoint no-filling problem was solved before this talk. The intended broader hypothesis set is not recoverable.

title: A shifted local zeta representative of the index density
notes: \(\alpha_0(x)=\zeta(D^*D+\varepsilon,x)-\zeta(DD^*+\varepsilon,x)\).
statement: For a closed elliptic operator, the difference of shifted local zeta values at zero integrates to its index. It equals the constant term in \(e^{-\varepsilon t}\) times the local heat supertrace. If negative-power supertrace coefficients vanish pointwise, as in the classical geometric Dirac case, this is the usual local index density; for a general elliptic operator the chosen local representative can depend on the shift.
reconstruction: We distinguish the shifted representative from a separately fixed canonical density and supply the suppressed evaluation at s=0.
fate: The heat-to-zeta relation in \citet[\S\S1.7 and 1.10]{gilkey1984invariance} and the spectral pairing in 1981-558.3 give this exact interpretation. Equality of integrals should not be strengthened into equality of all local representatives.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: the stated qualified result is established; the literal notebook shorthand should be read with the hypotheses above.

title: The corrected ray integral and the alleged Seeley sign error
notes: Equation (15) has \(+1/m\); equation (16), labelled correct, has \(-e^{i\theta}/m\) and \(b^\circ_{-m-n}(x,\xi,e^{i\theta}\lambda)\). The margin says Seeley has the wrong sign.
statement: The substitution from a ray variable \(z=e^{i\theta}\lambda\) contributes the factor \(e^{i\theta}\). A meaningful comparison must also fix whether the resolvent is \((A-z)^{-1}\) or \((z-A)^{-1}\), the orientation, trace/Fourier normalization and any kernel term. The scan supports the corrected minus sign and a zero first argument of the local zeta value, but does not by itself establish a publication error.
reconstruction: Only the ray substitution is convention-independent; the full formula is not silently normalized to agree with a modern source.
fate: \citet[\S2]{ponge2006spectral} state explicit complex-power and residue conventions. The original Seeley formula was not verified at this level in this run; the attribution of an error is consequently an unresolved lead rather than an endorsed correction to his paper.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: the stated qualified result is established; the literal notebook shorthand should be read with the hypotheses above.

title: The repeated div–grad–curl square
notes: The all-positive vector-calculus matrix is now explicitly on \(\mathbb R^3\), but is again said to square to \(\Delta I\).
statement: With standard Euclidean conventions, its vector block squares to \(2\operatorname{grad}\operatorname{div}-\Delta I_3\), not \(\Delta I_3\). Replacing the upper-right entry by \(-\operatorname{div}\) gives the self-adjoint elliptic matrix whose square is \(-\Delta I_4\).
reconstruction: The correction fixes a declared convention; the scan is transcribed faithfully.
fate: This is the same occurrence as the example in 1981-558.6, repeated a week later. The algebraic calculation is included with its independent polynomial-symbol check; \citet[Introduction]{atiyahpatodisinger1975spectral1} is the historical geometric context.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: the stated qualified result is established; the literal notebook shorthand should be read with the hypotheses above.
speaker: I. M. Gelfand

title: Differences of spectral-cut zeta functions at integer points
notes: For two rays of minimal growth, \(\rho(s)=\zeta_\theta(A,s)-\zeta_{\theta^{\prime}}(A,s)\) is meromorphic; its residues vanish microlocally at integral candidate poles and its integral-point values are local.
statement: Let \(P\) be a positive integer-order \(m\) classical elliptic operator on a closed manifold with two admissible spectral cuts, and let \(\Pi_{\theta,\theta^{\prime}}(P)\) be the associated sectorial projection. With arguments in \((\theta-2\pi,\theta)\), \[\rho(s)=(1-e^{-2\pi i s})\operatorname{TR}(\Pi_{\theta,\theta^{\prime}}P_\theta^{-s}).\] The factor cancels the possible simple pole at any integer \(k\), and \[\rho(k)=\frac{2\pi i}{m}\operatorname{Res}(\Pi_{\theta,\theta^{\prime}}P^{-k}).\] The residue is an integral of a local symbol density.
reconstruction: The canonical-trace notation and orientation convention are modern; the notebook’s sign in its symbol-residue formula is not compared without matching conventions.
fate: \citet[Theorem 4.2, equations (4.13)--(4.14)]{ponge2006spectral} prove this precise formulation and trace the method to Wodzicki. The 1982 paper was already published before the talks; the fuller 1984 treatment followed them. The primary Wodzicki publisher records were opened, but the exact original theorem text was unavailable, so priority between those two articles is not inferred from the notebook.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: The integer-value residue formula is established in the stated classical calculus; the microscopic cancellation and global integral are distinct statements.

title: Cut independence at zero and the nonpositive-integer extension
notes: Part (d) says \(\rho(\ell)=0\) for \(\ell=0,-1,-2,\ldots\), while the following hint mentions integers \(>0\).
statement: For admissible positive-order classical elliptic operators, \(\rho(0)=0\): the noncommutative residue of a pseudodifferential projection vanishes. At other integers, the exact criterion is \(\operatorname{Res}(\Pi P^{-k})=0\); it is not permissible to erase this condition for arbitrary classical pseudodifferential \(P\). The blanket nonpositive-integer assertion can fail even for differential operators: in odd dimensions, negative-integer poles of the absolute zeta or eta functions can give nonzero cut differences. Additional parity or residue-vanishing hypotheses are needed.
reconstruction: The valid zero-value theorem is separated from the false general extension. Regularity of a cut zeta function at a negative integer does not imply equality of its values for different cuts.
fate: \citet[Theorem 4.3 and Remark 4.5]{ponge2006spectral} verify zero-value cut independence. \citet[\S4]{loyamoroianu2012singularities} verify admissible negative poles for Dirac-type differential operators in odd dimensions; together with the cut-difference identity these rule out the unrestricted extension. An independent explicit check in \hyperref[dev:1981-negative-cut]{the spectral verification} constructs an invertible massive Dirac operator on the flat three-torus: its two cut zeta values at \(-1\) are \(\mp i\pi^2\mu^4\). The positive-integer hint conflicts with the displayed range and remains a source ambiguity.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: Cut independence at zero is established. The stated extension to every nonpositive integer is false without further restrictions, including within differential-operator settings.

title: The shifted-zeta polynomial and its missing powers
notes: For order one, equation (20) gives a binomial sum plus \[t^k\sum_{\mu=1}^n\frac{(-1)^\mu\delta_\mu}{\mu\binom{k+\mu}{k}},\] without \(t^\mu\) in its summands.
reconstruction: The complete corrected coefficient derivation is included as an annotation in the development file, not claimed as a new theorem of spectral theory.
fate: The correction follows by expanding \((A+t)^{-s}\) and taking the limit at \(s=-k\); the coefficient is independently checked symbolically in the included code. Wodzicki’s local-invariant programme is the historical context, but a direct published equation-by-equation match to (20) was not read. The literal omission is already contradicted by setting \(t=0\) when a residue is nonzero.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: The corrected local shift identity is verified under these hypotheses; the notebook formula without the additional powers is false.

title: The Mahler analogy and the unspecified p-adic continuation
notes: The first finite sum is called a Mahler transform; an automorphic function for it is said to continue to a p-adic domain.
statement: Mahler’s classical theorem expands a continuous \(f:\mathbb Z_p\to\mathbb Q_p\) in the binomial basis, with coefficients tending to zero. To turn the spectral shift identity into a p-adic interpolation statement one would need a specified p-adic coefficient field, sequence, continuity/congruence estimates and meaning of automorphy. None is supplied here.
fate: \citet{mahler1958interpolation} is a genuine antecedent for the binomial basis; the further automorphic/p-adic sentence cannot be matched to a precise theorem from the notes. No general p-adic continuation of spectral zeta values is asserted.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026: The Mahler basis theorem is established; the proposed spectral/automorphic continuation is not identifiable from the recorded data.
